text:
Semyon Varlamov kept the Islanders in this one far longer than the chances allowed. Ottawa generated 3.09 expected goals to New York's 1.83, and Varlamov's 19 shots faced were worth 2.09 more goals than he gave up. That gap showed up most in the second period, when OTT out-chanced NYI 1.75 to 0.76 in expected goals. Dylan Cozens had the best look of the night, a 25 percent chance that missed the net.

New York scored first, with Matias Maccelli beating Linus Ullmark on a wrist shot at 19:48 of the first from a chance worth 8 percent. Ridly Greig tied it at 15:43 of the second with a snap shot, set up by Warren Foegele and Artem Zub. Greig's line controlled play when he was on the ice, with 0.93 expected goals for against 0.24 against. Neither side scored on the power play, and OTT went 0 for 4 despite 1.37 expected goals on those chances.

The shootout turned on one shot. Drake Batherson, Tim Stützle, Brayden Schenn and Bo Horvat were all stopped, and Shane Pinto scored in the third round. Simon Holmstrom then failed to answer, and OTT won 2-1. By the deserved-to-win measure, OTT took 72 percent of simulated replays, so the extra point matched the play, even if Varlamov made it much harder than it should have been.
